1.web: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
1.asv: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.

2.web: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing, but the glory of kings is to search out a matter.
2.asv: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing; But the glory of kings is to search out a matter.

3.web: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, so the hearts of kings are unsearchable.
3.asv: As the heavens for height, and the earth for depth, So the heart of kings is unsearchable.

4.web: Take away the dross from the silver, and material comes out for the refiner;
4.asv: Take away the dross from the silver, And there cometh forth a vessel for the refiner:

5.web: Take away the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
5.asv: Take away the wickedfrombefore the king, And his throne shall be established in righteousness.

6.web: Don’t exalt yourself in the presence of the king, or claim a place among great men;
6.asv: Put not thyself forward in the presence of the king, And stand not in the place of great men:

7.web: for it is better that it be said to you, “Come up here,” than that you should be put lower in the presence of the prince, whom your eyes have seen.
7.asv: For better is it that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, Than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince, Whom thine eyes have seen.

8.web: Don’t be hasty in bringing charges to court. What will you do in the end when your neighbor shames you?
8.asv: Go not forth hastily to strive, Lestthou know notwhat to do in the end thereof, When thy neighbor hath put thee to shame.

9.web: Debate your case with your neighbor, and don’t betray the confidence of another;
9.asv: Debate thy cause with thy neighbor himself, And disclose not the secret of another;

10.web: lest one who hears it put you to shame, and your bad reputation never depart.
10.asv: Lest he that heareth it revile thee, And thine infamy turn not away.

11.web: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
11.asv: A word fitly spoken Islikeapples of gold in network of silver.

12.web: As an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, so is a wise reprover to an obedient ear.
12.asv: Asan ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, So isa wise reprover upon an obedient ear.

13.web: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to those who send him; for he refreshes the soul of his masters.
13.asv: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, So isa faithful messenger to them that send him; For he refresheth the soul of his masters.

14.web: As clouds and wind without rain, so is he who boasts of gifts deceptively.
14.asv: As clouds and wind without rain, So ishe that boasteth himself of his gifts falsely.

15.web: By patience a ruler is persuaded. A soft tongue breaks the bone.
15.asv: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded, And a soft tongue breaketh the bone.

16.web: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
16.asv: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, Lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

17.web: Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor’s house, lest he be weary of you, and hate you.
17.asv: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbor’s house, Lest he be weary of thee, and hate thee.

18.web: A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
18.asv: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbor Is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.

19.web: Confidence in someone unfaithful in time of trouble is like a bad tooth, or a lame foot.
19.asv: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble Islikea broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.

20.web: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
20.asv: As one that taketh off a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon soda, So is he that singeth songs to a heavy heart.

21.web: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink:
21.asv: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; And if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

22.web: for you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Yahweh will reward you.
22.asv: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head, And Jehovah will reward thee.

23.web: The north wind produces rain: so a backbiting tongue brings an angry face.
23.asv: The north wind bringeth forth rain; So doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance.

24.web: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than to share a house with a contentious woman.
24.asv: It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, Than with a contentious woman in a wide house.

25.web: Like cold water to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
25.asv: Ascold waters to a thirsty soul, So is good news from a far country.

26.web: Like a muddied spring, and a polluted well, so is a righteous man who gives way before the wicked.
26.asv: Asa troubled fountain, and a corrupted spring, So isa righteous man that giveth way before the wicked.

27.web: It is not good to eat much honey; nor is it honorable to seek one’s own honor.
27.asv: It is not good to eat much honey; Sofor mento search out their own glory is grievous.

28.web: Like a city that is broken down and without walls is a man whose spirit is without restraint.
28.asv: He whose spirit is without restraint Islikea city that is broken down and without walls.
